jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, AWS Vulnerability Management (AVM)
jobs.description: At Amazon, Security is our highest priority. Our team builds products and services to continuously identify, track, and mitigate security risks in third-party software and open source libraries across AWS. We work with the latest technologies and encourage a lifelong learning model. We are never bored and always have interesting and challenging tasks to solve. We're seeking an experienced Software Development Engineer to join our AWS Vulnerability Management team, responsible for building and maintaining critical security services that help protect AWS customers and infrastructure. Our team is at the forefront of cloud security, developing innovative solutions to identify and mitigate security risks before they can be exploited. You'll be handling complex challenges related to scaling vulnerability management across AWS's ever-growing infrastructure. This role offers the opportunity to: 1) Build next-generation vulnerability management systems that operate at cloud scale 2) Design and implement machine learning-based vulnerability prediction and prioritization mechanisms 3) Work directly with AWS service teams to integrate security controls and vulnerability assessments 4) Collaborate with world-class security engineers and researchers to stay ahead of emerging threats 5) Participate in the full software development lifecycle, from design through deployment and maintenance We are open to hiring candidates to work out of one of the following locations: Arlington , VA USA Seattle , WA USA Austin, TX USA Key job responsibilities Designing and building services that scale for millions of users and systems. Driving new innovation in the Amazon/AWS ecosystem and "Think Big!" Continually learn different technologies and architectures to ensure we have the correct solutions Java, Python, Big Data, Microservices etc. Solving complex problems with elegant solutions by working across teams and organizations in Amazon. Own your solutions and the entire life-cycle, from the roadmap to the architecture to implementation and continuous iterative development. A day in the life During a regular day engineers within our team work across multiple organizations and multiple technologies to ensure that AWS maintains the correct security posture. We partner with the compliance and application security teams to identify and work through any potentially impactful issues. We also define and maintain highly scalable solutions built on AWS Services to improve the visibility and tracking of security exposures worldwide. We have a mix of both new and tenured engineers that all bring a unique aspect with them to any challenge. The team is made up of Software Development Engineers, Security Engineers, and System Development Engineers all working together to ensure our solutions meet/exceed the needs of our customers and are scalable. About the team Diverse Experiences Amazon Security values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying. Why Amazon Security? At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores. Inclusive Team Culture In Amazon Security, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Ongoing DEI events and learning experiences inspire us to continue learning and to embrace our uniqueness. Addressing the toughest security challenges requires that we seek out and celebrate a diversity of ideas, perspectives, and voices. Training & Career Growth We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, training, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional. Work/Life Balance We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve. - 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience - 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience - Experience programming with at least one software programming language - 2+ years of Amazon experience, or experience with AWS services or other cloud offerings - 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience - 2+ years of track record of building and automating builder-facing security tooling and guardrails at scale Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Building Connectivity Engineering
jobs.description: Every Amazon data center runs on networks no customer ever sees: the corporate network that engineers and tools use to reach the fleet, the segmented networks that cameras and badge readers ride on, the network for building systems, and the isolated controls networks behind power and cooling. Building Connectivity Engineering (BCE), part of AWS Networking, owns the design and operation of those fabrics in every Amazon data center, and builds them into more than 100 new sites a year. Building Connectivity Software Systems (BCSS) is the software team inside BCE. We build the controller for these networks. It holds the intended state of every fabric as a model, computes everything a new site needs (addresses, routing identifiers, ports, cabling, device registration) before a technician plugs in the first rack, renders device configuration from the model, and drives the deployment and monitoring platforms that AWS Networking already runs. The first production release went live in September 2026 and took a site build that used to need about twenty hand-run steps down to one request. Most of the controller is still ahead of us. We are hiring Software Development Engineers to build the next releases: a versioned model of intended network state with full history and rollback, device configuration rendered from that model instead of written by hand, and the orchestration that takes a site from a plan to live traffic with one physical touch. You will design services, write the design documents for them, build them on AWS, prove them in shadow mode against real sites, and run them in production. The network engineers who hold the fabric knowledge are your partners; your code is the engine their models run on. Key job responsibilities * Design and build services in AWS (Lambda, Step Functions, DynamoDB, EventBridge, CDK), modeled with Smithy and deployed through pipelines you own. * Write the design document for what you build. Every engineer on this team writes designs; it is a core part of the job, and seniority is not the gate. * Integrate with the systems of record in AWS Networking (IP address management, device registry, routing-policy store, configuration store and release, deployment, cabling plans), and find out what each contract actually does, against the real service, before committing to a date. * Prove correctness in shadow mode: compute what the automation would do for a site, diff it against what engineers did by hand, and get to zero discrepancies before any cutover. * Own what you ship in production: metrics, alarms, runbooks, and a turn in the team's on-call rotation, which covers the new services and the ones the team inherited. * Keep fabric knowledge out of the code. New fabrics, site types and rack types arrive as models the network engineers author; your job is to make the second one cost a configuration change. * Estimate honestly: size work by how novel it is and how many systems outside the team it touches, raise partner asks early, and say what is unknown. A day in the life You pick up a card to add a new reservation type to the allocation service. Before writing code you spend an hour against the real partner API in a test account and find that the contract does not do what its wiki page says, so you write that down, re-size the card, and raise the ask with the partner team that morning instead of three weeks in. The afternoon is a design review of a teammate's state machine change, where the question you keep asking is what happens on the retry, and your own code review landing with its shadow-mode diff attached. A few times a year you are the on-call engineer for a week, and the team expects that week to be your work. About the team BCSS, formed in May 2026. We bring software engineering practice to a problem space that has not had software developers, and we never cut corners: slow is smooth, and smooth is fast. Our stance in one line is a team tenet: we don't just make a change, we make a changer. Our software runs on AWS and operates entirely detached from production data traffic. We work inside an operating model where network fabric teams run like software teams: they own their business logic, expose APIs, and measure outcomes. BCSS builds the software; every fabric team owns its automation roadmap and its adoption. Design reviews are open and argued; the best objection in the room wins, whoever raised it. - 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience - 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience - 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience - 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience - 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience - Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field - Experience programming with at least one software programming language - 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience - Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent - Experience architecting/operating solutions built on AWS - Experience owning and leading significant projects from concept to deployment - Experience working with networking fundamentals or Internet protocols such as TCP/IP, UDP, SSL, DNS, HTTP/S, or equivalent - Experience with workflow orchestration and event-driven designs (Step Functions, EventBridge or equivalents), including idempotency, retries and rollback - Experience integrating with systems whose APIs you do not control, and designing for their failure modes - Experience with data modeling: versioned data, graph-shaped data, or generating configuration or code from a model Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Navigation Experiences (NavX)
jobs.description: Would you like to innovate on the most visible and persistent experience on Amazon's websites and apps, one that reaches every customer who visits and supports partner teams across the company? Would you like to build low latency, highly resilient distributed systems at scale, and deliver world class customer experiences across every device? If so, the Navigation Experiences (NavX) team has an opportunity for you. NavX serves tens of thousands of transactions per second and billions of views per day. Our footprint is large and visible, and the systems behind it have to be fast, reliable, and easy for partners to build on. The role As a full stack Software Development Engineer on NavX, you will design, build, and operate both the backend services and the customer facing experiences that make up navigation across Amazon. You will own features and components end to end, from data model and service to the rendered experience on app, mobile web, and desktop. You will ship code daily through continuous deployment pipelines in an agile environment, and you will optimize our systems for scale, latency, and resilience. You will work closely with other engineers, product managers, and partner teams, and you will take technical ambiguity and turn it into concrete, well scoped designs. You will raise the engineering bar on the team through code reviews, operational excellence, and mentoring, and you will keep looking around the corner for ways to improve the architecture and the customer experience. What you will work on We own navigation across all devices on the Amazon retail experience. That includes browsing destinations in the Hamburger menu, shopping within Store Modes, finding account and personalized content in the You Tab, and discovering strategic programs through the Strategic Subnav and Discovery Bar. We own the navigation chrome on all rendering platforms, along with the platform aspects of its flyouts and tooltips. To support builders across Amazon, we also own Nav Config Studio, which lets partner teams specify navigation links and hierarchies through our experiences. Our mission is to serve as an indispensable guide that helps customers find what they need, whenever and wherever they need it, and to get out of the way when they do not need our help. Our vision is a tailored navigation experience that brings forward the most important and relevant information for a customer at any stage of their shopping journey. Key job responsibilities You have strong technical design, problem solving, and communication skills, and you are comfortable working with technical and non technical stakeholders. You have experience building and operating production cloud services, and you understand how to design for scalability, performance, and reliability. You are a full stack engineer who is as comfortable in a service and data layer as in the client code that renders a customer experience. You want to learn new skills and take on problems that have not been solved before, and you work backwards from the customer. About the team We are a diverse, intellectually curious team that likes to have fun and accomplish big things. We care about engineering excellence, operational ownership, and a customer experience we are proud of. - 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience - 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience - 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience - 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience - 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience - Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field - Experience programming with at least one software programming language - 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience - Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, EC2 UltraServer Availability
jobs.description: The Software Development Engineer II will design, build, and maintain cloud-based repair and recovery workflows for NVIDIA GB200 / GB300 UltraServers, orchestrating repair and recovery operations from impairment detection through completed recovery. This role requires expertise in AWS services, system architecture, and cross-functional collaboration with Capacity Management, Hardware Engineering, and Datacenter Operations to manage AI/ML infrastructure. Key job responsibilities The Software Development Engineer (SDE II) on the EC2 UltraServer Availability team is responsible for ensuring high availability of customer GB200 and GB300 UltraServers by orchestrating complex repair and recovery workflows. Following are the core responsibilities System Design & Architecture * Design and architect solutions that are cross-functional to Capacity Management, Hardware Engineering, and Datacenter Operations * Work in environments where the technology strategy is defined but the solution design is not * Build solutions that are stable, logical, testable, and efficient with the ability to independently make trade-off decisions * Investigate and develop design concepts to frame solution sets at an application and product level Software Development * Build cloud-based solutions using AWS native services for scaling infrastructure frameworks * Write high-quality, maintainable code with proper testing and code reviews * Develop and maintain the repair and recovery workflows for GB200 and GB300 UltraServer hosts * Implement automation for diagnostic triage, hardware testing, cable validation, and testing processes * Create observable systems with appropriate metrics and alarming Operational Excellence * Execute and monitor UltraServer workflows for UltraServer repair * Troubleshoot workflow failures and coordinate with downstream teams * Focus on operational excellence by identifying problems and proposing solutions Hardware & Software Integration * Work with hardware and software integrations specific to GPU clusters and AI/ML training systems * Manage network partition configurations for multi-node GPU clusters * Handle firmware validation and consistency checks across asset groups Team Collaboration * Collaborate with customers and stakeholders to convert business needs into technical designs * Participate in code reviews and technical assessments A day in the life This is a hands-on position in which you will own everything from end to end: requirements gathering, designs, design reviews, implementations, code reviews, incremental feature launches, operations, mentoring, and the driving of continuous improvement. About the team The EC2 UltraServer Availability team is a high-performing engineering organization responsible for maintaining high availability of NVIDIA-based ML infrastructure at scale. We manage end-to-end repair and recovery workflows for GB200 and GB300 UltraServers, from initial problem detection through repair and recovery. Our team drives operational excellence through continuous improvement of problem detection, repair efficacy, and customer impact mitigation. We work closely with hardware engineering, data center operations, and EC2 service teams to ensure reliable, efficient recovery of critical ML compute capacity. This is a high-impact role leading a two-pizza team of talented engineers solving complex technical challenges in one of Amazon's fastest-growing infrastructure domains. - 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience - 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience - Experience programming with at least one software programming language - 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience - Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent - Knowledge of professional software engineering & best practices for full software development life cycle, including coding standards, software architectures, code reviews, source control management, continuous deployments, testing, and operational excellence Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. jobs.title: Data Platform Software Engineer
jobs.description: It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started. Join us to put AI to work for people. Database Provisioning builds the tools that safely operate and manage the databases running in ServiceNow data centers, including RaptorDB, ServiceNow's PostgreSQL-based database. Internal operations and support teams use the CLI tools we create, and so does every automation running in a ServiceNow data center. Our challenge is to deliver high-quality solutions that run reliably, without interruption, at massive scale. Our work is fundamental to ServiceNow's reliability, reputation, and success. We believe ease of use, quality, scale, and customer feedback are the pillars of good development. We work in a very collaborative environment with distributed teams in the US and Europe. New team members are mentored in the skills they need to become strong contributors. What you get to do in this role Build and improve snc-provision, our in-house framework that deploys, configures and operates RaptorDB (PostgreSQL) and MariaDB databases in production, including the snow CLI used by operations teams and automation, and Dojo, our fleet-wide scheduled maintenance and monitoring service. Own well-scoped features from design through implementation, test automation and delivery, with guidance from senior engineers. Write clean, maintainable, well-tested code, and take part in code and design reviews. Automate operational tasks across a large database fleet, from configuration management to monitoring and remediation. Help investigate production issues, including database crashes, backup/restore failures and performance problems, and learn to drive root-cause analysis from logs, stack traces, and system data. Work with operations, support, and partner engineering teams to understand requirements and turn feedback into improvements. Contribute to documentation and runbooks, and share what you learn with the team. To be successful in this role you have A solid foundation in data structures, algorithms, and object-oriented design. Hands-on experience with Linux, and an interest in learning its internals. Familiarity with relational databases, ideally PostgreSQL, MySQL or MariaDB, and a desire to learn how they run in production. Strong problem-solving skills and curiosity about how systems fail. Clear communication, and comfort working with teammates across time zones (PT, ET, CET). Qualifications Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI's potential impact on the function or industry. Typically requires a bachelor's degree and a minimum of 2 years of related experience; or an advanced degree without experience; or equivalent work experience. Programming experience in Ruby, Python, Go or a similar language, plus shell scripting. Ruby is preferred but not required; engineers with Python or other scripting experience pick it up quickly. Experience with source control and CI/CD systems such as Git and Jenkins. Nice to have: Puppet or another configuration management tool; database backups, replication or high availability; Kubernetes; AI coding tools such as Claude Code, Windsurf or Cursor. Ability to work (hybrid model) out of either our San Diego, Santa Clara, or Kirkland office. Potential option to be remote. For positions in this location, we offer a base pay of $139,700 - $216,500 , plus equity (when applicable), variable/incentive compensation and benefits.
